name: Essent Preorder Back in Stock
summary: Shopify pre-order and back-in-stock app: presale and made-to-order campaigns with deposits and split payments, a Notify me waitlist with automatic restock emails, mixed-cart rules and market targeting, with plans tiered by monthly pre-orders and notifications.
best_for: Shopify stores running pre-orders, presales or made-to-order drops that also want a Notify me waitlist with restock emails in the same app, at a few hundred pre-orders a month or fewer, starting on a free plan that already takes deposits
skip_if: you hold stock in several locations and need pre-orders driven by one location's inventory, which a reviewer says the app does not do; you expect one launch to sell far past your plan's allowance and would rather pay a fixed price; or you only need a back-in-stock button and no pre-orders
honest_knock:
The plans are cheap until a launch works. Each paid plan has a monthly allowance and then charges per use: on Lite, the 101st pre-order in a month costs $0.25, and so does every one after it, so a drop that sells 300 pre-orders on Lite costs $4.95 plus $50 in overage. Starter at $8.95 would have covered those 300 without any. Restock alerts are metered the same way, at $1.00 per 100 past the allowance. Pick the plan on the size of the launch you are planning, not on an average month, and check the usage screen while a campaign runs. The free plan's 25 pre-orders is enough to test the flow end to end, and the listing does not say what happens when a free store passes it.

Two features stores often assume are basic sit higher up. Mixed-cart validation, which stops a shopper from putting an in-stock item and a pre-order item in one order, starts on Starter at $8.95, as do campaigns limited to specific markets. A pre-order confirmation email sent from your own domain and scheduled campaigns start on Lite.

The critical reviews are few but specific. A South African store six months in wrote in September 2025 that the app counts inventory across every location, so a store with stock in a physical shop cannot run pre-orders for its online warehouse alone; the developer replied in October 2025 that the request had gone to its development team. An Australian store wrote in June 2026 that after turning the app off with stock back in, its code stayed behind and blocked the checkout button for days; the developer replied after an internal investigation. A US store in August 2025 reported unreliable email delivery and that the pre-order status did not appear on the customer's order confirmation. Earlier one-star reviews describe the app putting every product on pre-order instead of the chosen one, a discount lost when a shopper changed size or quantity, and an admin that would not load; the developer answered each by offering support.

The long list of positive reviews deserves one note. Several reviews were written within the first hour of use, and one UK merchant asked the developer to prompt for a review after three days rather than one hour. The app asks for broad access too: the data-access section lists viewing sensitive customer data and editing customers, products, orders, Shopify Functions and the online store. We have not installed the app.

pricing.plans_source: summarised from pricing.notes; every plan name and amount appears verbatim in those notes
pricing.notes: (read 2026-10-04 on apps.shopify.com/essential-pre-order, pricing table and data-access section; the vendor's own pricing page at essential-apps.com/pricing lists the apps but no prices) Four plans on the listing plus an unlimited plan mentioned on the top card, priced on two meters: pre-orders a month and back-in-stock notifications a month. Free covers 25 pre-orders and 300 back-in-stock notifications a month, with unlimited Notify me sign-ups, automated pre-orders and restock alerts, variant-level campaigns, full and partial payments, customisable buttons, forms and emails, and 24/7 support. Lite is $4.95 a month for 100 pre-orders and 1,000 notifications, and adds translations, a pre-order confirmation email sent from your own domain, scheduled pre-order campaigns, the Omnisend and Shopify Flow integrations and premium support. Starter is $8.95 a month for 300 pre-orders and 2,500 notifications, and adds campaigns limited to specific markets and mixed-cart validation, with all features unlocked. Essentials is $24.95 a month for 500 pre-orders and 10,000 notifications, with priority support. Past the allowance each paid plan charges per use: $0.25 per extra pre-order on Lite, $0.20 on Starter and $0.10 on Essentials, and $1.00 per 100 extra notifications on all three. The Essentials card adds that unlimited volume is available on a Professional plan at $59 a month. Paid plans carry a 14-day free trial. The listing does not say what happens on the free plan past 25 pre-orders. All charges are in USD; recurring and usage charges are billed through Shopify every 30 days. Developer Essential Apps, with an address in Vilnius, Lithuania; the listing gives a launch date of 22 November 2024 and shows 1,291 reviews, eleven of them at three stars or lower.

compare_with.name: Timesact Preorder
compare_with.why: Timesact Preorder is the closest app in our own dossiers. On our reading of 25 September 2026 Timesact's free plan covered 20 orders a month, its usage-based CORE Flexible plan started at $5 a month for 10 orders and $17 for 100, with $0.20 per order past the volume you pick, and its CORE Fixed plan covered unlimited orders for $23 a month on a Basic Shopify store, rising to $117 on Shopify Plus. Essent Preorder Back in Stock, read on 4 October 2026, gives 25 pre-orders and 300 restock alerts free, 100 pre-orders for $4.95 and 300 for $8.95, with unlimited volume on a $59 Professional plan. At low and medium volume Essent is the cheaper of the two; a Basic Shopify store that regularly passes a few hundred pre-orders a month pays less on Timesact's fixed plan. Both bundle back-in-stock alerts with pre-orders and take deposits.
